headline: WhatsApp Must Be Tied to Your Phone's SIM From 1 January 2027

image.author: Paowee
image.size: 3840x3720 (Commons rendition of the 4273x4140 original, fetched via Special:FilePath?width=2560)
image.subject: Samsung Galaxy A02s (dual-SIM) with its SIM tray ejected, showing two SIM cards and a microSD card; ICCID and numbers partly edited out by the author

fact_sources.fact: From 1 Jan 2027, messaging apps that sign users up by phone number must work only while the registered SIM is present and active in the device (SIM binding)
Compliance deadline extended to 31 Dec 2026; operational from 1 Jan 2027
Could be cut off: Wi-Fi-only tablets/spare phones without the SIM; phones whose registered SIM is removed, swapped or lapsed (not recharged)
Apps named in DoT's Nov 2025 directions include WhatsApp, Telegram, Signal, Arattai, ShareChat, Josh, JioChat (and Snapchat, which says it is not covered)
Government's stated reason: accounts kept working after the SIM was removed, deactivated or moved abroad, letting scammers misuse Indian numbers
The fixed 6-hour web logout was dropped; web/desktop logouts will be risk-based
The Nov 2025 directions gave apps 90 days to comply (120 days to report); the deadline was later extended to 31 Dec 2026
